what_it_measured.text: The purpose of this study was to investigate the ability of recombinant human thymosin β4 (rhTβ4) to promote healing in a benzalkonium chloride (BAC)-induced mice DED model and the anti-inflammatory effects involved in that process.
As expected, NF-kB thy,activation we investigated NF-kB activation in rhTβ4 treatment groups.

dose.text: Eye drops consisting of 0.05% and 0.1% rhTβ4 were used for treatment of DED.

route.text: topical administration of the corresponding concentrations of rhTβ4 solution (5µL/eye) four times a day (9:30 a.m., 11:30 a.m., 14:30 p.m., and 17:30 p.m.) for 7 days.

endpoint.text: Tear volume and corneal staining scores were measured after 7 days.
The red portion of the thread was measured in millimeters.

Measurement of Tear Production The number of tears was measured with the phenol red thread tear test using cotton threads (Tianjin Jingming New Technology Development Co., LTD, Tianjin, China) at day 7.

reported_results.text: Mechanically, the rhTβ4 groups showed significantly reduced inflammatory cytokine levels and CD4+ T cells in conjunctiva by blocking NF-κB (nuclear factor kappa B) activation, suggesting that 0.05–0.1% rhTβ4 eye drops may be used as a potential therapeutic treatment for DED.
All clinical parameters showed improvement in both the 0.05% and 0.1% rhTβ4 groups.
The rhTβ4 groups showed an improvement in all clinical parameters compared with the BAC group. ** p < 0.01.
The rhTβ4 groups had a lower number of TUNEL positive cells cornea compared with the BAC group. n = 6 mice per group, * p < 0.05; ** p < 0.01.
Notably, no greater advantage was observed in 0.1% rhTβ4 group compared to the 0.05% rhTβ4 group.
As expected, NF-kB activation was induced in the BAC group, and was significantly reduced when treated with 0.05% and 0.1% rhTβ4 (Figure 5A,B).
